content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sodium teriyaki sauce is a flavorful Asian condiment made from soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, ginger, and garlic, but with less salt (≈ 0.5 g per 100 ml). It gives dishes a sweet‑salty taste without overwhelming them with sodium.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The lower sodium level is achieved by replacing part of the salt with potassium chloride or using naturally low‑salt fermented soybeans.
Teriyaki sauce is commonly used as a glaze or marinade for meat, fish, tofu, and vegetables.
Sugar in the sauce can be swapped for honey, maple syrup, or stevia for a healthier version.
Homemade teriyaki allows precise control over salt and sugar content.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Soy sauce, the base ingredient, provides plant‑based protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Ginger and garlic are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Ginger stimulates gastric secretions, aiding digestion.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Reduced salt makes the sauce more suitable for people monitoring blood pressure.

items.title: Flavorful with fewer calories
items.content: The sweet‑salty profile lets you use less sauce, saving calories.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to soy should avoid this sauce.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite lower sodium, the sauce may still contain notable sugar, important for diabetics.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
items.content: Some commercial versions add MSG, which can cause sensitivity in certain people.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Sugar and oil add calories; moderate consumption is advised.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use the sauce as a marinade for meat, fish, or tofu, as a glaze when grilling, pan‑frying, or baking, and stir it into rice, noodle dishes, or salads. It also works well as a dip for vegetables and sushi rolls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Refrigerate after opening in a tightly sealed bottle. Keep for up to 3 months. Discard if color, smell, or taste changes.
